summary: A one-line correction to the network mail meeting announced in RFC 453: the SRI-ARC meeting moves to Friday, February 23, 1973 at 8:30 AM, with Saturday as a possible second day. It is a schedule notice only.

plainLanguage.summary: A note saying the meeting about sending letters between computers has been moved to a different day.

subtitle: A rescheduled meeting to discuss network email protocols.

tldr.problem: A working group had scheduled a meeting to design a network mail system, but the original date needed to be changed.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 456 announced that the meeting had been rescheduled to Friday, February 23, 1973 at 8:30 AM at SRI-ARC, with Saturday as a backup day if a second day was needed.
tldr.outcome: The meeting proceeded at the new time to discuss what would become one of the early network mail protocols.

today: RFC 456 updates RFC 453 with a new meeting date. It is a historical record of early coordination in designing network mail protocols.

sections.title: Meeting Rescheduled
sections.content: RFC 456 announces a change to the schedule of a Network Mail System working group meeting originally announced in RFC 453. The new meeting date was Friday, February 23, 1973 at 8:30 AM, held at the SRI-ARC Conference Room.
sections.plainLanguage: The network mail meeting was moved to Friday, February 23rd.

sections.title: Backup Plan
sections.content: The RFC notes that if a second day was needed to complete the discussions, the group would meet on Saturday, February 24th. This flexibility allowed the working group to resolve all necessary issues without being constrained by a single-day schedule.
sections.plainLanguage: If they could not finish on Friday, they would meet again on Saturday.

sections.title: Early Network Mail Development
sections.content: This meeting was part of the early effort to standardize how electronic mail could be transmitted over the ARPANET. The design of network mail protocols was a significant undertaking that required coordination among multiple research sites. The flexibility to extend the meeting to a second day reflected the complexity of the problem and the importance of reaching consensus on design decisions.
sections.plainLanguage: The working group was trying to figure out how to send mail between computers on the network, and this meeting was part of that effort.
